page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with an exceptionally high memory capacity of 336.0 GB, translating to 84.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Local storage is bundled with a 945 GB disk, and the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The server achieves top-tier single-core Geekbench and text processing scores, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. Conversely, multi-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks falling into the weak category. Memory performance also shows a clear tradeoff: cached small-block read-only bandwidth is average at 345.84 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, measuring 36.33 GB/sec and 25.55 GB/sec respectively. LLM inference speeds are average for small models but drop to poor for larger models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX16-4mds_v2 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads. By pairing a massive 336.0 GB RAM footprint with only 4 vCPUs, it allows organizations to run memory-heavy applications without paying for unnecessary CPU cores, which is highly advantageous for software with per-core licensing models. This configuration is best suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching systems like Redis, single-threaded data processing tasks, and memory-bound enterprise applications that require high single-core clock speeds but low parallel processing overhead.
